summary: Executed the edge-ablation control on the 11-entity linked fixture. In the baseline, four subject IDs, the alias actor, and the composing merge subject shared one token, while the account and four households had distinct tokens. Removing the second cross-tenant link split only the third subject; the other three subject IDs, alias actor, and merge subject stayed together. Removing the composing merge row split only the merged subject; the other subject IDs, alias actor, and linked third subject stayed together. Account and household tokens were identical across all three runs, and the person class never collapsed into the account class. All seven expected checks passed. This shows that the link and merge edges are load-bearing and that unrelated components are not over-merged, but it is a small fixture-level control, not a full-corpus ablation. Evidence strength is causal at fixture scale; the official verifier was not run.
next_hint: The union edges are causally load-bearing at fixture scale. The remaining uncertainty is host-side official verification and the hidden interpretation of effective-dated merges, noise scaling, and token length.
